content.text: Databases are the foundation of virtually every production system, providing durable storage, efficient retrieval, and transactional guarantees for application data. Modern backend engineers must understand relational databases across the spectrum — from universal SQL fundamentals through PostgreSQL's advanced extension ecosystem and Oracle's enterprise-grade clustering and diagnostics — as well as document databases like MongoDB with their flexible schemas and horizontal scalability. The choice between SQL and NoSQL is rarely binary; most production systems use multiple database technologies, selecting the right tool based on data access patterns, consistency requirements, and scaling needs. PostgreSQL has become the default choice for new applications requiring complex queries, JSONB flexibility, and strong consistency, while Oracle remains dominant in enterprise environments demanding extreme availability and complex transactional workloads. Understanding the trade-offs between these systems, their unique optimization strategies, and their operational characteristics is essential for designing data layers that perform at scale.

This multi-page guide covers database technologies from fundamentals through advanced performance optimization, targeting senior engineers who need to design schemas, tune queries, and operate databases at scale. Each subtopic provides production-oriented depth with real-world examples, common failure modes, and interview preparation material.

items: SQL Fundamentals — Core SQL concepts across all databases: joins, subqueries, CTEs, window functions, and stored procedures
PostgreSQL — Extensions, MVCC, advanced indexing (GIN, GiST, BRIN), JSONB, partitioning, replication, and connection pooling
Oracle Database — PL/SQL, RAC, Data Guard, flashback technology, AWR/ASH diagnostics, and enterprise partitioning
MongoDB and Document Databases — Document modeling, aggregation pipelines, indexing strategies, and replica set operations
SQL Performance Tuning — Query plan analysis, indexing strategies, partitioning, and query optimization techniques
Database Design Patterns — Schema design, normalization, denormalization, and data modeling for different workloads
Transactions and Consistency — ACID properties, isolation levels, distributed transactions, and eventual consistency patterns
